meaning.en: To feel that a short parting has lasted very long, because one misses the other so much.
meaning.zh: 形容思念殷切，觉得分别的时间很长。

equivalents: a day apart seems like three years

examples.zh: 才分开三天，我就如隔三秋，天天盼着你回来。
examples.en: We have only been apart three days, but it feels like an age and I wait daily for you to return.

examples.zh: 出差一个月，对家人的思念让他如隔三秋。
examples.en: During a month-long business trip, missing his family made it feel like three years.

examples.zh: 两位老友虽只别了数月，却如隔三秋。
examples.en: Though the old friends had been apart only a few months, it seemed like years.

story.en: The Book of Songs poem 'Picking Kudzu' sings "a day without seeing you is like three autumns" (一日不见，如三秋兮).
story.zh: 《诗经·王风·采葛》：“一日不见，如三秋兮。”

date.zh: 西周至春秋 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: Western Zhou to Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: Predicate or complement; affectionate, often about lovers or close friends. Usually 一日不见，如隔三秋.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、补语；感情色彩浓，多用于恋人或挚友，常说“一日不见，如隔三秋”。

meaning.en: Neither ancient nor modern; an awkward mixture that fits no style.
meaning.zh: 既不像古代的，也不像现代的，形容不伦不类。

equivalents: an awkward hybrid of old and new

examples.zh: 这座新建的仿古楼不古不今，很难看。
examples.en: This newly built imitation-antique building is neither old nor new and rather ugly.

examples.zh: 他穿一身不古不今的衣服出现在聚会上。
examples.en: He turned up to the party in an outfit that was neither period nor modern.

examples.zh: 这种装修风格不古不今，让人摸不着头脑。
examples.en: This decor style is a muddle of eras that leaves people puzzled.

usage.en: Mostly attributive or predicate, about clothes, architecture, writing or style; mildly mocking.
usage.zh: 多作定语或谓语，形容服饰、建筑、文风等；略带讥讽。

meaning.en: Unwilling to lag behind others; eager to be in the lead.
meaning.zh: 不甘心落在别人后面。

equivalents: determined to keep up with the best

examples.zh: 同学们个个不甘后人，都在埋头苦读。
examples.en: Every classmate was unwilling to fall behind and was studying hard.

examples.zh: 他不甘后人，主动申请了最难的项目。
examples.en: Unwilling to lag behind, he volunteered for the hardest project.

examples.zh: 各国都不甘后人，竞相发展新能源。
examples.en: Each country, unwilling to be left behind, is racing to develop new energy.

usage.en: Predicate; positive, expresses competitive drive. Also written 不甘人后.
usage.zh: 多作谓语；含褒义，表示争强好胜；也作“不甘人后”。

meaning.en: Troops who are elderly, weak or disabled, thus of little fighting strength.
meaning.zh: 年老体弱或伤残的士兵，指战斗力很差的军队。

equivalents: a ragged band of the old and wounded

examples.zh: 城里只剩下一些老弱残兵，根本守不住。
examples.en: Only a few old and wounded soldiers remained in the city, and it simply could not be held.

examples.zh: 敌军主力已被击溃，余下的不过是老弱残兵。
examples.en: The enemy's main force had been routed, and what remained was merely old and crippled troops.

examples.zh: 球队只剩几个老弱残兵，比赛还怎么打？
examples.en: The team has only a few old and injured players left; how can it play the match?

usage.en: Noun phrase, also used humorously of a depleted team or company.
usage.zh: 名词性短语，也可戏指人手不足、状态不佳的队伍。

meaning.en: Natural justice and one's conscience; often invoked as an appeal: 'in all conscience'.
meaning.zh: 指天道公理和人的良心，常用来表示凭良心说话或做事。

examples.zh: 你摸着天理良心说，这事是不是你的错？
examples.en: Put your hand on your heart: wasn't this your fault?

examples.zh: 做人要讲天理良心，不能昧着良心赚钱。
examples.en: One must act by conscience and not earn money by going against it.

examples.zh: 他说他对得起天理良心，一点也不心虚。
examples.en: He said he had acted in all conscience and felt no guilt at all.

usage.en: Often used in oaths or appeals (凭天理良心, 讲天理良心); colloquial and emotional.
usage.zh: 常用于发誓或质问（凭天理良心、讲天理良心）；口语，情绪色彩强。

meaning.en: Success in office, reputation and riches, the worldly goals people chase.
meaning.zh: 功业、名声、财富和地位，指世俗追求的目标。

examples.zh: 他看淡功名富贵，选择隐居山林。
examples.en: He took a light view of fame and fortune and chose to live as a hermit in the hills.

examples.zh: 功名富贵不过是过眼云烟。
examples.en: Fame and wealth are only passing clouds.

examples.zh: 为了功名富贵，他不惜出卖朋友。
examples.en: For the sake of fame and fortune he did not hesitate to betray his friends.

usage.en: Noun phrase, often as object of 追求/看淡/贪图; neutral to slightly critical.
usage.zh: 名词性短语，常作“追求、看淡、贪图”的宾语；中性略带贬义。

natural: a single stroke opens the heavens

meaning.en: The legendary first trigram stroke drawn by Fu Xi at the dawn of civilisation; figuratively, a pioneering beginning.
meaning.zh: 传说伏羲画下第一画八卦，开启了文明，比喻开创性的起点。

examples.zh: 相传伏羲一画开天，奠定了《易经》的基础。
examples.en: Legend says Fu Xi's first stroke opened the heavens and laid the foundation of the Book of Changes.

examples.zh: 这项发明有一画开天的意义。
examples.en: This invention is of pioneering significance.

examples.zh: 文字的诞生，堪称一画开天之举。
examples.en: The birth of writing can be called a pioneering first stroke.

usage.en: Literary, referring to the legend of Fu Xi's first hexagram stroke; used metaphorically for epoch-making starts.
usage.zh: 书面语，源于伏羲画八卦的传说；比喻开天辟地的创始。

natural: not content to stay at home

meaning.en: Not content to stay at home; restless. In older use, said of a wife who does not behave properly in the household.
meaning.zh: 不安心在家里待着，不安分。旧时多指已婚女子不守本分。

examples.zh: 他生性不安于室，总想出去闯荡。
examples.en: By nature he can't stay at home and always wants to go out and make his way.

examples.zh: 这位年轻人不安于室，辞掉工作去环游世界。
examples.en: The young man was restless and quit his job to travel the world.

examples.zh: 旧小说里常骂不安于室的女子，这种观念早已过时。
examples.en: Old novels often censure women who are 'not content to stay at home'; that idea has long been outdated.

usage.en: Predicate; literary. The traditional sense is sexist and now outdated; the neutral 'restless' sense is safer.
usage.zh: 多作谓语；书面语。旧义含性别偏见，现已过时；表示“不安分”的中性用法较稳妥。

meaning.en: To act promptly as soon as one sees the opportunity.
meaning.zh: 一看到时机就立即行动。

examples.zh: 他见机而作，趁对手松懈时果断出手。
examples.en: He seized the moment and struck decisively when his opponent relaxed.

examples.zh: 做生意要见机而作，不能犹豫。
examples.en: In business you must act when the chance appears; no hesitation.

examples.zh: 大军见机而作，一举攻下了城池。
examples.en: The army acted as soon as it saw its chance and took the city in one move.

story.en: The Appendix to the Book of Changes says "the gentleman acts upon seeing the subtle sign, without waiting a whole day" (君子见几而作，不俟终日).
story.zh: 《周易·系辞下》：“君子见几而作，不俟终日。”

usage.en: Predicate; literary, close to 见机行事 but stresses starting action at once rather than adapting step by step.
usage.zh: 多作谓语；书面语，与“见机行事”相近，更强调抓住时机立即行动。

meaning.en: Luxurious carriages and splendid horses; a rich, lavish way of life.
meaning.zh: 华美的车子和骏马，形容富贵奢华的排场。

examples.zh: 他出入都是香车宝马，排场十足。
examples.en: He goes everywhere in luxury cars and with a great show.

examples.zh: 她羡慕香车宝马的生活，却忽视了背后的代价。
examples.en: She envied the life of luxury cars and glamour but overlooked the cost behind it.

examples.zh: 电视剧里的香车宝马吸引了不少观众。
examples.en: The luxury cars in the TV series drew many viewers.

usage.en: Noun phrase for opulence; literary but common in modern writing, sometimes mildly critical.
usage.zh: 名词性短语，形容奢华；书面语，现代文章也常用，有时略含批评。

meaning.en: To hesitate and not dare to go forward.
meaning.zh: 犹豫徘徊，不敢向前。

examples.zh: 面对新的机会，他趑趄不前，错失良机。
examples.en: Faced with a new opportunity he hung back and missed it.

examples.zh: 别再趑趄不前了，大胆去尝试吧。
examples.en: Stop hesitating and boldly give it a try.

examples.zh: 队伍在河边趑趄不前，不敢涉水。
examples.en: The party hesitated at the riverside, not daring to wade across.

usage.en: Predicate; literary. 趑趄 is a rare bound word, so mostly seen in this set phrase.
usage.zh: 多作谓语；书面语。“趑趄”是生僻词，多见于此成语。

meaning.en: So tightly packed or sealed that not even wind can get through.
meaning.zh: 严密得连风都透不过，形容包围、防守等非常严密。

equivalents: packed so tightly that nothing gets through

examples.zh: 警方把现场围得密不通风。
examples.en: The police sealed the scene airtight.

examples.zh: 车厢里挤得密不通风，大家喘不过气。
examples.en: The carriage was so packed that no air could get through and everybody was gasping.

examples.zh: 他们的防守密不通风，对手无从下手。
examples.en: Their defence was airtight and the opponents had no way in.

usage.en: Predicate or complement; used for crowding, defence, secrecy or sealing.
usage.zh: 多作谓语或补语；形容拥挤、防守、保密严密。

natural: sun and moon crossing the sky

meaning.en: Of lasting glory, as constant and bright as the sun and moon crossing the heavens.
meaning.zh: 像日月运行于天空一样，比喻光辉永存、功绩长久。

equivalents: as eternal as sun and moon

examples.zh: 先贤的功绩如日月经天，永远照耀后人。
examples.en: The achievements of the ancient sages are like the sun and moon in the sky and shine on later generations forever.

examples.zh: 他的文章如日月经天，影响了几代人。
examples.en: His writing, like the sun and moon in the sky, influenced several generations.

examples.zh: 这些原则日月经天，不可动摇。
examples.en: These principles are everlasting and unshakeable.

usage.en: Mostly in the pattern 如日月经天 or paired with 江河行地; for deeds, ideas and reputations that last.
usage.zh: 多见于“如日月经天”，常与“江河行地”对举；形容功绩、思想、声誉长久。

pinyin: bàn bù lún yǔ zhì tiān xià
literal: half · volume · Analects · govern · the world
natural: half the Analects can govern the world

meaning.en: Even half of the Analects is enough to run the empire: a short classic well understood goes a long way.
meaning.zh: 据说宋代赵普说，只用半部《论语》就能治理天下；比喻学问贵精，真正读懂一点经典就足够受用。

equivalents: a little classic wisdom goes a long way

examples.zh: 半部论语治天下，读书重在领会，而不在多。
examples.en: Half the Analects can govern the world: in reading, understanding matters more than quantity.

examples.zh: 老校长常说半部论语治天下，让学生把基础经典读透。
examples.en: The old headmaster often said that half the Analects could govern the world, urging students to read basic classics thoroughly.

examples.zh: 半部论语治天下，这话说明经典的价值。
examples.en: 'Half the Analects can govern the world' shows the value of the classics.

story.en: Luo Dajing's Southern Song notes record the story that the chancellor Zhao Pu said he had used half the Analects to help the first emperor win the empire and would use the other half to bring peace to the next.
story.zh: 南宋罗大经《鹤林玉露》载赵普对宋太宗说：“臣平生所学，唯《论语》一部，以半部佐太祖定天下，以半部佐陛下致太平。”

usage.en: Proverb-like; quoted when praising classics or deep reading over wide reading.
usage.zh: 似谚语；多用于称赞经典，强调读精读透。

pinyin: wú yuán zhī shuǐ, wú běn zhī mù
literal: no · source · 's · water · no · root · 's · tree
natural: water without a source, a tree without roots

meaning.en: Something with no foundation will not last; an idea or work without basis is empty.
meaning.zh: 没有源头的水、没有根的树，比喻没有基础、没有根据的事物不能长久。

equivalents: water without a spring, tree without roots

examples.zh: 脱离实践的理论是无源之水，无本之木。
examples.en: Theory divorced from practice is water without a source and a tree without roots.

examples.zh: 没有文化积累的创新，只是无源之水，无本之木。
examples.en: Innovation without cultural accumulation is just a stream without a spring and a tree without roots.

examples.zh: 这种说法毫无依据，是无源之水，无本之木。
examples.en: This claim has no basis at all; it is rootless.

usage.en: Used in argument, as a verdict on baseless ideas; often split into 无源之水 and 无本之木.
usage.zh: 用于议论，评价缺乏根据的观点；也常拆开单用“无源之水”“无本之木”。

meaning.en: Stirring up trouble out of nothing; making a fuss where there is no cause.
meaning.zh: 没有风也能掀起三尺高的浪，比喻无中生有、无事生非。

examples.zh: 他总爱无风三尺浪，把小事闹得沸沸扬扬。
examples.en: He loves to stir up trouble out of nothing and blows small things up into a big scene.

examples.zh: 别信他的话，那人向来无风三尺浪。
examples.en: Don't believe what he says; that man always makes trouble out of nothing.

examples.zh: 公司本来平静，他一来就无风三尺浪。
examples.en: The company had been calm, but as soon as he came he stirred up waves.

usage.en: Colloquial; criticising someone who invents disputes. Not the same as 无风不起浪, which means rumours have some basis.
usage.zh: 口语；批评无事生非的人。与“无风不起浪”（传闻总有缘由）意思不同。

meaning.en: When one has too many troubles or debts, one stops feeling them.
meaning.zh: 虱子多了就不觉得痒，比喻困难或债务多了，反而不觉得担心。

equivalents: when problems pile up you stop minding

examples.zh: 他欠的债太多，已经虱多不痒了。
examples.en: He owes so much already that he has stopped worrying.

examples.zh: 问题一个接一个，虱多不痒，也就麻木了。
examples.en: Problems came one after another; with so many, he went numb.

examples.zh: 你已经被批评那么多次，真是虱多不痒。
examples.en: You've been criticised so often that you're quite indifferent.

usage.en: Colloquial, often wry; usually paired with 债多不愁.
usage.zh: 口语，常带自嘲；多与“债多不愁”连用。

pinyin: yǒu zhì bù zài nián gāo
variants: 有志不在年高，无志空活百岁
literal: have · ambition · not · lie in · age · high
natural: ambition does not depend on age

meaning.en: What matters is having ambition, not being old: the young can achieve great things.
meaning.zh: 有志气不在于年纪大，年轻人同样能成就大事。

equivalents: youth is no bar to achievement

examples.zh: 有志不在年高，这个十二岁的孩子已经拿了全国大奖。
examples.en: Ambition has no age: this twelve-year-old has already won a national prize.

examples.zh: 别小看年轻人，有志不在年高。
examples.en: Don't underestimate young people; ambition is not a matter of age.

examples.zh: 有志不在年高，他十八岁就创办了自己的公司。
examples.en: He started his own company at eighteen, proving ambition has nothing to do with age.

usage.en: Used to encourage the young; often paired with 无志空活百岁.
usage.zh: 用来鼓励年轻人；常与“无志空活百岁”连用。

pinyin: féng shān kāi lù, yù shuǐ dā qiáo
literal: meet · mountain · open · road · meet · water · build · bridge
natural: cut a road at mountains, build a bridge at rivers

meaning.en: Whatever obstacle appears, find a way past it.
meaning.zh: 遇到山就开路，遇到水就架桥，比喻不畏艰难，想办法克服一切障碍。

equivalents: cross each bridge as you come to it
find a way round every obstacle

examples.zh: 创业就是逢山开路，遇水搭桥。
examples.en: Starting a business means clearing a path wherever there is a mountain and building a bridge at every river.

examples.zh: 地质队员逢山开路，遇水搭桥，把设备运进了深山。
examples.en: The geological team cut roads through mountains and bridged rivers to bring the equipment deep into the hills.

examples.zh: 别怕困难，我们逢山开路，遇水搭桥。
examples.en: Don't fear difficulties; we'll make a road at every mountain and a bridge at every river.

usage.en: Used literally for engineers and explorers, figuratively for tackling obstacles; encouraging tone.
usage.zh: 可指工程、勘探，也比喻克服困难；有鼓励意味。

pinyin: yǒu zéi xīn méi zéi dǎn
literal: have · thief's · heart · lack · thief's · nerve

meaning.en: To have bad intentions but lack the courage to carry them out.
meaning.zh: 心里有坏念头，却没有胆量去做。

examples.zh: 他有贼心没贼胆，只敢在背后说坏话。
examples.en: He has the thoughts but not the nerve, and only dares to bad-mouth people behind their backs.

examples.zh: 这种人就是有贼心没贼胆，不足为惧。
examples.en: That kind of person has wicked ideas but no nerve and isn't to be feared.

examples.zh: 他想偷懒，可有贼心没贼胆，怕被老板发现。
examples.en: He wanted to slack off but lacked the nerve, afraid the boss would notice.

usage.en: Colloquial, mocking; sometimes said jokingly about harmless temptations.
usage.zh: 口语，带嘲讽；有时也用于开玩笑，指无伤大雅的念头。

variants: 人善被人欺，马善被人骑
literal: person · kind · be · by people · bullied

meaning.en: Too gentle a person is taken advantage of by others.
meaning.zh: 为人善良软弱，容易被人欺负。

examples.zh: 人善被人欺，你再不硬气点，他们还会得寸进尺。
examples.en: The kind get bullied; if you don't toughen up they will push their luck.

examples.zh: 老实人吃亏，人善被人欺，这话不是没有道理。
examples.en: The honest lose out and the kind get bullied; there's something in that saying.

examples.zh: 他总觉得人善被人欺，所以对谁都很强硬。
examples.en: He always believes the kind get bullied, so he is tough with everyone.

usage.en: Colloquial; often followed by 马善被人骑; a worldly-wise warning, not an endorsement of cruelty.
usage.zh: 口语，常接“马善被人骑”；是世故的告诫，并非鼓励刻薄。

pinyin: yī xiè bù rú yī xiè
literal: one · crab · not as good as · one · crab
natural: each crab worse than the last

meaning.en: Each one is worse than the one before.
meaning.zh: 一个比一个差。

examples.zh: 这几任经理一蟹不如一蟹。
examples.en: These last few managers have each been worse than the one before.

examples.zh: 这几部续集一蟹不如一蟹，口碑越来越差。
examples.en: The sequels got worse one after another and their reputation kept sinking.

examples.zh: 这个月的饭菜一蟹不如一蟹。
examples.en: The meals this month have each been worse than the last.

usage.en: Colloquial, criticising a series of successors or products.
usage.zh: 口语，批评一连串继任者或产品质量下降。

natural: no one knows a son like his father

meaning.en: A father knows his own son best.
meaning.zh: 最了解儿子的人是他的父亲。

equivalents: a father knows his son best
no one knows a child like a parent

examples.zh: 知子莫若父，他想要什么，老爸一猜就中。
examples.en: A father knows his son best; Dad guesses what he wants right away.

examples.zh: 知子莫若父，您说得对，他确实没有恒心。
examples.en: A father knows his son; you're right, he really lacks perseverance.

examples.zh: 俗话说知子莫若父，可这回他爸也没猜对。
examples.en: As the saying goes, a father knows his son best, but this time even his dad guessed wrong.

usage.en: Often paired with 知臣莫若君 (a ruler knows his ministers); used when parents judge their children.
usage.zh: 常与“知臣莫若君”连说；用于父母判断子女时。

story.en: The Guanzi (Da Kuang) has the line "No one knows a son like his father, no one knows a minister like his ruler." The proverb takes its first half.
story.zh: 《管子·大匡》有"知子莫若父，知臣莫若君"之语。俗语"知子莫若父"即取其前半句。

date.zh: 战国至西汉 · 前4世纪—前1世纪
date.en: Warring States to Western Han, 4th–1st c. BC

pinyin: xiù cái zào fǎn, sān nián bù chéng
literal: scholar · rebel · three · years · not · succeed
natural: scholars rebel, and take three years to fail

meaning.en: Scholars are too talk-heavy and indecisive to carry out a revolt; theorists rarely get things done.
meaning.zh: 读书人造反，三年也成不了事，比喻书生只会空谈，缺乏行动力。

equivalents: bookish people can't carry out bold action

examples.zh: 他们光开会不行动，真是秀才造反，三年不成。
examples.en: They hold meetings but never act; truly scholars staging a revolt that takes three years to fail.

examples.zh: 别指望研究生搞经营，秀才造反，三年不成。
examples.en: Don't expect academics to run a business; scholars rebel and three years pass in vain.

examples.zh: 这个团队全是书呆子，秀才造反，三年不成，也难怪项目迟迟没进展。
examples.en: This team is full of bookworms, so little wonder the project hasn't progressed.

usage.en: Colloquial, mildly mocking, about people who plan and talk but do not act; the sense is not literal.
usage.zh: 口语，带调侃，指光谈计划不行动的人；并非字面义。

pinyin: quán bù lí shǒu, qǔ bù lí kǒu
literal: fist · not · leave · hand · tune · not · leave · mouth
natural: keep fists in practice and songs on the lips

meaning.en: Skills must be practised constantly to stay sharp.
meaning.zh: 练拳要经常练，唱曲要经常唱，比喻技艺必须天天练习，才不会生疏。

examples.zh: 拳不离手，曲不离口，他每天坚持练琴两小时。
examples.en: He practises two hours daily: keep your fists in training and songs on your lips.

examples.zh: 拳不离手，曲不离口，歌手半个月不唱就退步了。
examples.en: A singer who doesn't sing for a fortnight gets worse.

examples.zh: 老师总说拳不离手，曲不离口，基本功天天练。
examples.en: The teacher always says to practise fundamentals daily, as fists must not leave the hand.

usage.en: Quoted when urging daily practice in martial arts, opera, music and other crafts.
usage.zh: 用于劝人天天练习武术、戏曲、音乐等技艺。
